label: assertion
text: Across extensive experiments on CIFAR-100, TinyImageNet, and CIFAR-10 using standard architectures and a broad set of unstructured sparsification methods, sparse neural networks trained on challenging samples often achieve test accuracy that matches or surpasses the corresponding dense models at particular overall sparsity ratios in the 10%–90% range.

label: assertion
text: The behavior described in 【5】 is observed for clean test accuracy.

label: assertion
text: The behavior described in 【5】 is observed, in adversarial training regimes, for adversarial accuracy (accuracy on perturbed test data) as well.

label: assertion
text: When training data are scarce (where the data ratio, the fraction of the challenging subset used for training, is reduced from the full set), sparse neural networks tend to outperform dense counterparts more markedly than in the full-data regime.

label: assertion
text: When training data are scarce, the advantage of sparse neural networks over dense counterparts is most pronounced at higher overall sparsity levels in the reported experiments.

label: assertion
text: Under adversarial training with Projected Gradient Descent (PGD), sparse models at high sparsity achieve comparable clean test accuracy compared to dense models on the examined benchmarks (VGG16 on CIFAR-10 and ResNet18 on CIFAR-100).

label: assertion
text: Under adversarial training with Projected Gradient Descent (PGD), sparse models at high sparsity achieve superior adversarial test accuracy compared to dense models on the examined benchmarks (VGG16 on CIFAR-10 and ResNet18 on CIFAR-100).

label: assertion
text: This trend, described in 【1, 8】, holds at both full and reduced data volumes tested in the paper.

label: assertion
text: Sparse methods that allocate higher relative density (proportion of non-zero weights) to early (shallower) layers tend to yield higher test accuracy on hard-sample training than uniform per-layer pruning.

label: 论据
text: Empirically, layer-wise density profiles (proportion of non-zero weights) with richer shallow-layer connectivity correlate with improved performance across training on EL2N-selected samples, corrupted images with common corruptions, and adversarial training scenarios (using PGD).

label: assertion
text: Methods that derive sparse topologies from pre-trained dense models can tolerate sparser shallow layers

text: In the studied setup (one-shot pruning at initialization with rewinding to t=0), LTH sometimes exhibits degraded performance when trained on hard samples

label: assertion
text: masks produced from dense pre-training are not universally optimal for hard-sample regimes

label: assertion
text: whether a sparse method starts from a pre-trained dense model or from scratch materially affects performance on hard samples and interacts with the layer-wise density allocation

label: assertion
text: Dynamic-sparse training methods that form sparse topologies before or early during training achieve the dual benefit of test accuracy improvement and reduced training floating-point operations and parameter counts in the evaluated hard-sample regimes (EL2N-selected, corrupted, adversarial).

label: assertion
text: Dense-to-sparse procedures that require obtaining a fully trained dense model incur additional training floating-point operations (FLOPs) due to dense pre-training.

label: assertion
text: The sparse models resulting from dense-to-sparse procedures that require obtaining a fully trained dense model may have fewer parameters.

label: assertion
text: When training on inputs corrupted by common visible degradations, using 30% of the corrupted subset (a training data ratio of 0.3), the relative benefit of sparse neural networks (SNNs) over dense models grows as corruption severity increases from low to moderate levels (severity 2 to severity 4 on the 1–6 scale).

label: assertion
text: At extreme corruption severity (severity 6), the relative improvement of sparse neural networks (SNNs) over dense models shrinks or disappears for some sparse methods.
